findings.section: Why this shape, and what was rejected / Out of scope
findings.summary: C2 closes the hole where a word is matched as written for $, but brace expansion and globs belong to the same class and stay open. The brief neither covers them nor names them out of scope.
findings.evidence: Today's binary: `vloop fence check --phase review --tool bash 'git pu{sh,} origin'` -> allow, and `git {push,status}` -> allow; `bash -c 'echo git pu{sh,} origin'` prints `git push pu origin`. A glob (`git pu?h` with a file named push in the cwd) expands the same way. internal/fence/judge.go `match` joins the words as written.
findings.fix: The operator decides: (a) widen C2 so that a word holding an unquoted `{…,…}`/`{a..b}`, `*`, `?` or `[` also stands for any text, with worked-example lines; or (b) add it to Out of scope with a new issue. Recommended: (a) for braces at least, since `git pu{sh,} origin` is a real bypass of the review fence today.

findings.summary: The rule 'an option before the name holds v or V' also matches `-$v`, which holds a literal v. With v=p, `command -$v git push` runs git push and would be allowed.
findings.evidence: C3: "an option before the name holds `v` or `V` (`-v`, `-V`, `-pv`)"; today `command -$o git push` -> deny (looked through, judge.go skipDashes). A plain ContainsAny(opt, "vV") check would allow it.
findings.fix: Pin the option literally: a word of `-` followed only by the letters `p`, `v` and `V`, with at least one `v` or `V` (no `$`, no other letters). Add `command -$v git push` -> deny (by the review fence, Bash(git push:*)) to the worked example and to the planted failures.

findings.summary: The line template `vloop fence check … "<command>"` breaks for lines that hold `"` or `$`: the outer shell expands them, so the close task's run 'line for line through the built binary' tests a different command.
findings.evidence: `… "git diff "$BASE" --stat"` reaches the judge as `git diff  --stat` ($BASE is empty) -> allow, not the deny the line pins. The same happens to `"$tool"`, `"$f"`, `"$x"` and `"$gate_status"`.
findings.fix: Write the template as `vloop fence check --root <tmp> --phase <phase> --tool bash '<command>'`, with each inner `'` written as `'\''`, or state that the command is passed as one argument exactly as shown, never through shell interpolation.

findings.summary: The `for` bullet lists `for ((…))` among the forms answering `shell syntax for cannot be judged`, but the splitter refuses that `(` first, and the worked example pins `subshells and process substitution cannot be judged`.
findings.evidence: C1 subshell rule: `(` opens a subshell only after opening keywords, and `for` is not one. Worked example: `for ((i=0; i<3; i++)); do ls; done → deny: subshells and process substitution cannot be judged`. Today's binary gives the same answer.
findings.fix: Drop `for ((…))` from the `for` bullet, or note that it answers the subshell message because the splitter refuses it first.

findings.summary: The brief says `env ! x` is judged as a command named `!`, as today. Today it is denied as a keyword.
findings.evidence: `vloop fence check --phase review --tool bash 'env ! x'` -> `deny: shell syntax ! cannot be judged` (judge.go: the keywords map holds "!" and is checked after wrappers).
findings.fix: State the intended answer: either keep today's answer (`shell syntax ! cannot be judged`, which follows from the decided order) or say that it changes, and add the line to the worked example.

findings.summary: The denial counts are credited to the wrong runs and sections of the cited document. Two other figures cannot be checked from the repository.
findings.evidence: docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md: 5 `if` + 1 subshell is B24's section (line 365), not B26's; B26 (line 433) has 4 `for` + 1 `$(…)`; 1 `if` + 1 `for` matches B27 (line 477), while B29 (line 511ff) records 0 denials; 2 `if` is the gpt-6.1-terra planning section (line 568); B32's section (663ff) records no denial counts. Neither `command -v curl` nor the '52 shell calls in 7 kept sessions, 5 hold a $' figure appears in any file of the repository (grep).
findings.fix: Re-attribute the counts (B22.0, B24, B26, B27, the gpt-6.1-terra planning test), and cite those sections in the binding reference. Record the B32/B33 session figures (the `command -v curl` denial and the 52/5 count) in copilot-cli-experiments.md, or say where they come from.

findings.summary: The message says 'the command as written', but the worked example shows the words joined with their quotes stripped (`git $x origin` for `git "$x" origin`).
findings.evidence: C2: "The message is the rule's, with the command as written"; worked example: `for x in push; do git "$x" origin; done → deny: git $x origin is denied …`; judge.go `match` uses strings.Join(ws, " ").
findings.fix: Say "with the command's words joined by spaces, as today".

findings.summary: The new text for configuration.md gives `shell syntax case cannot be judged` as the sample answer, but a real `case` (with its `)` patterns) answers the subshell message.
findings.evidence: Worked example: `case x in a) ls;; esac → deny: subshells and process substitution cannot be judged`.
findings.fix: Use `[[` as the example: "answering `shell syntax [[ cannot be judged` (or the syntax at hand)".

decisions: Drop the leading keyword and judge the rest instead of parsing the grammar (mvdan.cc/sh rejected). Agree: nothing inside is judged less than one command per line.
case, select, function, coproc and [[ stay refused. Agree; none appears among the recorded denials.

A $ word stands for any text, accepting over-denials. Not listed in the brief: in a work session `rm "$f"` becomes denied (rm -rf:* matches), and so do `git log "$x"`/`git show "$x"` in every phase. Acceptable, but the operator should know.
A $ inside single quotes is literal. Agree.
command -v / -V only (type, which and hash need nothing). Agree, provided the option is pinned (see the C3 finding).
Subshells are read, not only braces; $(, <( and >( stay refused. Agree.
Order inside a command: opening keywords dropped first, then closing keywords/for/refused words, then assignments and wrappers. Agree.
`!` after a wrapper is not a keyword. Its stated answer contradicts today's (see the fact finding).
C2 applies in every phase and after every wrapper, the command name excluded. Agree.
Whether brace expansion and globs join C2 or go out of scope: not decided in the brief (see the ASK finding).
